item.text: I’ll inspect the workspace, then implement and test `merge_files.py` with an external-sort path so the memory limit is respected. I’ll also create a virtual environment and include `requirements.txt`.

The workspace is empty, so I’m adding a self-contained standard-library implementation. The design uses a two-pass scan only when schema inference is needed, then sorted spill chunks plus a heap-based merge; this keeps row data bounded by the configured memory budget.

The first implementation is in place. I’m now running focused checks for numeric ordering, null placement in both directions, timestamp normalization, schema projection, and forced multi-chunk merging; I found that sort keys need typed comparison separate from their serialized CSV representation, so I’m correcting that before finalizing.

item.text: A merge test exposed a real serialization issue when reading successive spill records: each chunk needs one persistent pickle reader because pickle memo state can span records. I’m fixing that and rerunning the full checks; the cast-failure behavior itself is correctly producing a nonzero exit and stderr diagnostic.

item.text: The corrected implementation now passes the focused checks: inferred union/lexicographic schema order, numeric ascending and descending sort, stable duplicate keys, null ordering, schema-based casting/projection, UTC timestamp output, and fail-on-cast-error diagnostics. The virtual environment is created and the dependency file is standard-library-only.

The tool supports schema inference, casting, null handling, stable composite sorting, external spill/merge sorting under memory limits, custom CSV options, and cleanup of temporary resources.
